2. Medication List

Prescriptions, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, and supplements. Update it whenever a medicine starts, stops, or changes dose. Bring it to every appointment.

  • Copy the name and strength straight from the label — include inhalers, eye drops, creams, patches, and herbal supplements.
  • Cross out old rows instead of erasing them; you may need the history later.
  • Questions for your pharmacist or provider: Can I take this with my other medicines? What side effects should I watch for? What do I do if I miss a dose?

Never start, stop, or change a dose without talking to your prescriber. Education only — not medical advice.

3. Immunization Tracker

Record vaccines so you and your care team know what you've had and when you're due for more. Ask your provider or pharmacy for a printout of your immunization record to fill this in accurately.

Pneumococcal (pneumonia)
Hepatitis B
HPV
MMR
Varicella (chickenpox)

Common adult vaccines to ask about: flu (yearly), COVID-19, Tdap/Td booster (every 10 years), shingles (age 50+), pneumococcal (age 65+, or younger with certain conditions). Vaccine timing depends on your age, health history, and risk factors — talk to your care team.

5. Request-Records Letters

You generally have the right to see and get copies of your own medical records under HIPAA. Fill in the blanks, keep copies of everything you send, and send requests by certified mail or through the patient portal so you have proof of delivery. Providers may charge a reasonable copying fee and often have up to 30 days to respond.

Letter 1 — Request my complete medical records

     

[Provider or facility name]
Attn: Medical Records / Health Information Management
(street address)
(city, state ZIP)

Re: Request for medical records    Patient:    Date of birth:
Medical record number (if known):

To Whom It May Concern:

I am requesting a complete copy of my medical records, including office visit notes, test results, imaging reports, immunization records, medication lists, and discharge summaries, from (date range).

Please send the records to:
(your name)
(street address)
(city, state ZIP)
or through my patient portal:

If you require a signed authorization form, please let me know and I will complete and return it promptly. Please contact me at with any questions or if there are fees associated with this request.

Thank you for your help.

Sincerely,


________________________________ (your signature)
(your printed name)

Send copies of everything you mail, and keep proof of delivery.

Letter 2 — Request records from a specific visit or date range

Use the same format as Letter 1, but open with:

"I am requesting copies of my medical records related to treatment for between and , including ."

Letter 3 — Request records be sent to another provider

Use the same format as Letter 1, but send the records directly to:

[Provider name]
(street address)
(city, state ZIP)
Fax:

I authorize the release of my records to this provider for continuity of care.
Signature:    Date:

Tips for requesting records

  • Include your full name, date of birth, and dates of treatment so records are easy to locate.
  • Ask for records in the format you want (paper or electronic). Electronic copies are often free or cheaper.
  • If a provider denies your request, you can ask for the reason in writing and file a complaint with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office for Civil Rights at hhs.gov/ocr.
  • To request records for someone else (a child, parent, or person you care for), you'll usually need proof of guardianship or a signed authorization from them.

Education only — not legal or medical advice. Records-request rights vary by situation and state. Asdale Dynamics, LLC is not a law firm or healthcare provider.
